THE OFFICE OF THE NATIONAL                                SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF VIETNAM
              ASSEMBLY                                          Independence - Freedom – Happiness
                --------                                                   ---------------
                No. 106/VBHN-VPQH                                                              Hanoi, May 19, 2026


                                                              LAW

                                                        LEGAL AID

  The Law on Legal Aid No. 11/2017/QH14 dated June 20, 2017 of the National Assembly, which comes into
  force from January 01, 2018 is amended by:

  1. The Law on Prevention and Combat of Human Trafficking No. 53/2024/QH15 dated November 28, 2024 of
  the National Assembly, which comes into force from July 01, 2025;

  2. The Law on Juvenile Justice No. 59/2024/QH15 dated November 30, 2024 of the National Assembly, which
  comes into force from January 01, 2026;

  3. The Law No. 05/2026/QH16 dated April 23, 2026 of the National Assembly on amendments to some articles
  of the Law on Legal Aid, which comes into force from January 01, 2027.

  Pursuant to the Constitution of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam;

  The National Assembly promulgates the Law on Legal Aid[1].

  Chapter I

                                                GENERAL PROVISIONS

  Article 1. Scope

  This Law provides for legally-aided persons; legal aid-providing organizations; legal aid-providing persons;
  legal aid services and responsibilities of agencies, organizations and individuals in legal aid services.

  Article 2. Legal aid

  Legal aid means provision of legal services free of charge to legally-aided persons in a legal aid-related case in
  accordance with this Law, contributing to protection of human rights and citizenship to access to justice and
  equality to the law.

  Article 3. Principles of legal aid services

  1. Compliance with law and professional regulations on legal aid.

  2. Timeliness, independence, honesty and respect for objective truth.

  3. Best protection of legitimate rights and interests of legally-aided persons.

  4. Non-collection of fees, economic benefits or other benefits from legally-aided persons.

  Article 4. Legal aid policies

  1. It is the State's responsibility to provide legal aid.

  2. The State shall have policy on protection of the rights to receive legal aid suitable for the economic-social
  conditions

  3. The State shall have policy on enhancement of the legal aid quality and attraction of resources to deliver legal
  aid services.

  4. The State shall support, encourage, record and honor agencies, organizations and individuals involved in legal
  aid services.

  Article 5. Financial sources used for legal aid

  1. Financial sources for the legal aid services include state budget; contributions and donations of foreign and
  domestic organizations, individuals and other lawful capital sources.

  2. [2] Funding from the state budget is included in the annual state budget estimate of the legal aid authority in
  accordance with Laws on budget, public investment, science, technology and innovation, digital transformation,
  digital technology industry, and relevant specialized laws.

  Local governments that have not balanced their budgets shall prioritize the allocation of budget from annual
  budget balancing transfers to support the settlement of typical or complex legal aid-related cases.

  3. Funding for legal aid services of voluntary organizations shall be guaranteed by such organizations.

  Article 6. Prohibited acts in legal aid services

  1. Legal aid-providing organizations and individuals must not commit the following acts:

  a) Infringe upon the dignity, honor or legitimate rights and interests of legally-aided persons; discriminate
  against legally-aided persons;

  b) Receive or demand any sum of money, economic benefits or other benefits from legally-aided persons; harass
  legally-aided persons;

  c) Disclose information on legal aid-related cases or legally-aided persons unless it is agreed in writing by
  legally-aided persons or otherwise provided for by law.

  d) Refuse or discontinue the provision of legal aid services, except for cases specified in this Law and
  regulations on procedures;

  dd) Abuse legal aid services for self-seeking activities, encroach on national security and defense, disturb social
  order and safety, cause adverse impacts on social ethics;

  e) Incite, provoke legally-aided persons to declare and supply false information and documents or to make
  complaints or denunciations or initiate lawsuits in contravention of law.

  2. Legally-aided persons, agencies, organizations and individuals engaged in legal aid services must not commit
  the following acts:

  a) Violate health, life, dignity, honor of legal aid-providing persons and the reputation of organizations providing
  legal aid services;

  b) Deliberately provide false information and documents on legal aid-related cases;

  c) Threaten, obstruct or illegally interfere in legal aid services; disturb, cause troubles and seriously violate
  regulations at legal aid-providing places.

  Chapter II

       LEGALLY-AIDED PERSONS, RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF LEGALLY-AIDED PERSONS

  Article 7. Legally-aided persons [3]

  1. People with meritorious services to the revolution; biological fathers, biological mothers, spouses, and
  children of martyrs and persons who had fostered martyrs.

  2. People in poor households and near-poor households.

  3. People infected with dioxin.

  4. Disabled people.

  5. Children.

  6. Ethnic minority people permanently residing in areas with exceptionally difficult socio-economic conditions;
  ethnic minorities with very small populations.

  7. Monthly social allowance beneficiaries who are elderly persons, victims of domestic violence in domestic
  violence cases, HIV-positive people.

  8. Low-income employees who are the accused or the victims.

  9. Persons facing unexpected hardships due to natural disasters or fires and receiving legal aid in cases directly
  related to remedy to consequences caused for them by such natural disasters or fires.

  10. Persons from full 16 to under 18 years old who are denuncees, persons proposed for prosecution, persons
  held in emergency cases, the accused, victims, witnesses, persons serving diversion measures, or inmates in
  accordance with regulations of the Law on Juvenile Justice.

  11. Victims, persons undergoing identification of victims of human trafficking, and accompanying individuals
  under 18 years of age in accordance with the Law on Prevention and Combat of Human Trafficking.

  12. Aggrieved individuals who do not hire defenders of their legitimate rights and interests in accordance with
  the Law on State Compensation Liability.

  13. Foreigners who are eligible for legal aid under international treaties to which the Socialist Republic of
  Vietnam is a signatory.

  14. Other legal aid beneficiaries in accordance with regulations of law.

  Article 8. Rights of legally-aided persons

  1. Have the right to receive legal aid services without paying fees, economic benefits or other benefits.

  2. Request legal aid by themselves or via their relatives, agencies, authorities and persons given jurisdiction to
  institute proceedings, authorities and persons instituting proceedings[4] or other agencies, organizations and
  individuals.

  3. Be informed about the right to receive legal aid services, procedures of legal aid when going to a legal aid-
  providing organization and concerned regulatory agencies.

  4. Request confidentiality of contents of legal aid-related cases.

  5. Select one local legal aid-providing organization and person in the list published; request change of legal aid-
  providing person when he/she falls into one of the cases specified in clause 1 and 2, Article 25 of this Law.

  6. Modify or withdraw legal aid requests.

  7. Be compensated for damages in accordance with law.

  8. Lodge complaints or denunciations about legal aid in accordance with this Law and other relevant Law.

  Article 9. Obligations of legally-aided persons

  1. Supply documents proving their eligibility for legal aid.

  2. Cooperate, sufficiently and promptly provide information, documents and evidences in respect of legal aid-
  related cases and be responsible for the accuracy of these information, documents and evidences.

  3. Respect legal aid-providing organizations, legal aid-providing persons and other agencies, organizations and
  individuals involved in legal aid-related cases.

  4. Do not request another legal aid-providing organization to provide legal aid for the case for which another
  legal aid-providing organization is providing legal aid.

  5. Comply with the Law on Legal Aid and rules of places of legal aid provision.

  Chapter III

       LEGAL AID-PROVIDING ORGANIZATIONS, RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF LEGAL AID-
                             PROVIDING ORGANIZATIONS

  Article 10. Legal aid-providing organizations

  1. Legal aid-providing organizations include state legal aid centers and legal aid-participating organizations.

  2. The Department of Justice shall announce a list of qualified local legal aid-providing organizations and post it
  on the website of the Department of Justice and send it to the Ministry of Justice to aggregate and post the list on
  the website of the National Law Portal[5].

  Article 11. State legal aid centers

  1. State legal aid centers are public service providers affiliated to the Department of Justice established by the
  provincial People’s Committee, have legal status, their own seals, head offices and accounts.

  2. [6] State legal aid centers may have branches

  Branch is an affiliate of a state legal aid center. The State legal aid center shall be responsible for all activities of
  its branch. Based on local socio-economic conditions and legal aid needs, the Chairperson of provincial People's
  Committee shall decide the establishment of branches of state legal aid centers.

  3. [7] The Government shall provide specific regulations on organization and operation of state legal aid centers
  and their branches; procedures for establishment, dissolution and merger of branches of state legal aid centers.

  Article 12. Legal aid-participating organizations

  1. Legal aid-participating organizations include organizations signing contracts to provide legal aid services and
  organizations registering for participation in legal aid services.

  2. Organizations signing contracts to provide legal aid services include law-practicing organizations and legal
  counseling organizations signing contracts with the Department of Justice to provide legal aid services in
  accordance with this Law.

  3. Organizations registering for participation in provision of legal aid services include law-practicing
  organizations and legal counseling organizations registering for participation in legal aid services according to
  this Law.

  Article 13. Rights and obligations of legal aid-providing organizations

  1. Legal aid-providing organizations shall have the following rights and obligations:

  a) Provide legal aid services;

  b) Request concerned agencies and organizations to cooperate and supply information and documents on legal
  aid-related cases;

  c) Pay compensations for damage caused by a member of such organization's faults during the process of
  providing legal aid services;

  d) Make reports, release statistics and communication on legal aid;

  dd) Settle complaints according to regulations of clause 2, Article 45 of this Law;

  e) Make recommendations to competent regulatory agencies on matters related to the settlement of legal aid-
  related cases.

  2. Legal aid-providing organizations shall have the following rights and obligations:

  a) Rights and obligations according to regulations of clause 1, this Article;

  b) Perform other tasks in legal aid requested or authorized by competent authorities.

  3. Organizations signing contracts to provide legal aid services shall have the following rights and obligations:

  a) Rights and obligations according to regulations of clause 1, this Article;

  b) Receive remunerations and costs for participating in legal aid-related cases in accordance with regulations of
  the Government;

  c) Other rights and obligations in accordance with the legal aid contract.

  4. Organizations registering for participation in provision of legal aid services shall have the following rights and
  obligations:

  a) Rights and obligations according to regulations of clause 1, this Article;

  b) Provide legal aid services in accordance with registered contents.

  Article 14. Legal aid-providing contracts

  1. Legal aid-providing contract shall be signed between the Department of Justice and the law-practicing
  organizations, the legal counseling organization, and between state legal aid center with legal aid supporting
  lawyer or for the provision of legal aid services in accordance with the civil law.

  2. Based on legal aid needs and actual conditions at the province, the Department of Justice shall select and sign
  a legal aid-providing contract with an organization that wishes to sign and meet the following requirements:

  a) The registered line of business shall correspond to the field of legal aid as specified herein;

  b) Act as law-practicing organization, legal counseling organization that has at least 01 legal counselor with at
  least 02 years of experience in consultancy or 01 full-time lawyer working at such organization;

  c) The facility shall be suitable for legal aid services;

  d) The organization has not been incurring an administrative penalty for violations against regulations on law
  practicing and legal counseling.

  3. Based on legal aid needs and resources to provide legal aid at the province, the provincial state legal aid center
  shall select and sign a legal aid-providing contract with a lawyer that meets the following requirements:

  a) He/she has not been incurring an administrative penalty for violations against regulations on law practicing;

  b) He/she has not been banned or restricted from carrying out professional activities under a decision of the
  competent authority;

  c) He/she has not been facing a prosecution for criminal liability;

  d) He/she receives a written approval from the law-practicing organization where he/she is working or the
  agency, organization that signs the labor contract with such lawyer.

  4. The provincial state legal aid centers shall select and sign legal aid-providing contracts with legal aid
  supporting collaborators as prescribed in Article 24 hereof.

  5. Organizations and individuals committed prohibited acts defined in clause 1 Article 6 hereof shall not select
  and sign legal aid-providing contracts within at least 02 years since the conclusion of the violation is issued.

  6. The Minister of Justice shall elaborate this Article.

  Article 15. Registration for participation in legal aid services

  1. Law-practicing organizations and legal counseling organizations which volunteer to provide legal aid with
  their own resources may register for participation in the provision of legal aid services as follows:

  a) Law-practicing organizations shall satisfy all conditions prescribed in point a, c and d clause 2 Article 14
  hereof;

  b) Legal counseling organizations shall satisfy all conditions prescribed in point a, c and d clause 2 Article 14
  hereof and have at least 01 legal counselor with 02 years of experience in consultancy or 01 full-time lawyer
  working at such organization

  2. Law-practicing organizations and legal counseling organizations shall register their scope, form, field and
  legally-aided persons with provincial Department of Justice that has granted their licenses for operation
  registration.

  3. The Minister of Justice shall stipulate procedures for registration for participation in the provision of legal aid
  services.

  Article 16. Termination of provision of legal aid services by legal aid-participating organizations

  1. Organizations signing contracts to provide legal aid services shall terminate their provisions of legal aid
  services in the following cases:

  a) Have no longer satisfied one of the conditions for signature of contracts for provision of legal aid services as
  prescribed in clause 2 Article 14 hereof;

  b) Terminate the provision of legal aid services under the contract;

  c) Cause serious consequences when providing legal aid services;

  d) Have their operation terminated in accordance with law.

  2. An organization registering for participation in the provision of legal aid services shall terminate its provision
  of legal aid services in the following cases:

  a) Has no longer satisfied one of the conditions for registering for participation in the provision of legal aid
  services as prescribed in clause 1 Article 15 hereof;

  b) It terminates its participation in legal aid services itself after sending a written notification to the provincial
  Department of Justice that has granted its license for operation registration;

  c) It has not provided legal aid services for 02 consecutive years except for cases due to objective reasons;

  d) It has caused serious consequences when providing legal aid services;

  dd) It has its operation terminated in accordance with law.

  3. When terminating provision of legal aid services, the legal aid-participating organization shall send a written
  notification to the Department of Justice and transfer dossiers of legal aid-related cases that it has not finished to
  the state legal aid center assigned by the Department of Justice for continuation in handling.

  Chapter IV

    LEGAL AID-PROVIDING PERSONS, RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF LEGAL AID-PROVIDING
                                     PERSONS

  Article 17. Legal aid-providing persons

  1. Legal aid-providing persons include:

  a) Legal aid assistants;

  b) Lawyers providing legal aid services under contract with State legal aid center; lawyers providing legal aid
  services assigned by legal aid-participating organizations;

  c) Legal counselors with at least 02 years of experiences in legal counseling service and working in legal aid-
  participating organizations;

  d) Legal aid collaborators.

  2. The Department of Justice shall announce a list of local legal aid-providing persons and post it on the website
  of the Department of Justice and send it to the Ministry of Justice to aggregate and post the list on the national
  law portal[8].

  Article 18. Rights and obligations of legal aid-providing persons

  1. Legal aid-providing persons shall have the following rights and obligations:

  a) Provide legal aid services;

  b) Be guaranteed to provide independent legal aid, not jeopardized, hindered, harassed or unlawful intervened;

  c) Refuse or discontinue the provision of legal aid services in cases specified in clause 1, 2 Article 25, clause 1
  Article 37 hereof and regulations on procedures;

  d) Be trained in legal aid knowledge and skills;

  dd) Ensure the quality of legal aid services;

  e) Comply with regulations on provisions of legal aid services;

  g) Strictly comply with rules of places of legal aid provision;

  h) Compensate or reimburse the amount of money already paid by the legal aid-providing organization to the
  damage sufferer due to his/her fault upon the provision of legal aid services in accordance with law.

  2. Legal aid assistants shall have the following rights and obligations:

  a) Rights and obligations according to regulations of clause 1, this Article;

  b) Participate in training courses to enhance knowledge and skills required in professional legal aid;

  c) Perform other tasks as assigned;

  d) Be entitled to regimes, policies, and incentives[9] as prescribed.

  3. Lawyers and legal aid collaborators who enter into contracts with state legal aid centers for provision of legal
  aid shall be entitled to remuneration and expenses for the provision of legal aid according to regulations.

  4. The Government shall elaborate point d clauses 2 and 3 this Article.

  Article 19. Conditions to be satisfied by legal aid assistants [10]

  Vietnamese citizens who are public employees of legal aid centers and fully satisfy the following conditions may
  become legal aid assistants:

  1. Have good moral quality;

  2. Possess a bachelor or higher degree in law;

  3. Have been trained in legal profession or is not required to participate in training course of legal profession;

  4. Have gone through the probation of legal profession or legal aid, except for those who used to be legal aid
  assistants;

  5. Be physically fit to provide legal aid.

  Article 20. Legal aid trainee

  1. Public employees of the state legal aid center possessing certificates of lawyer profession training or
  exempting from law practice training according to the Law on Lawyers may register for legal aid training at state
  legal aid center.

  The legal aid training probation duration is 12 months. The state legal aid center shall assign legal aid assistants
  to provide guidance for legal aid trainee and admit the legal aid training probation. Guidance-providing legal aid
  assistants shall have at least 03 years of experience in assisting legal aid. At a time, a legal aid assistant must not
  provide guidance for more than 02 trainees.

  2. The legal aid trainee may assist the legal aid assistant in their professional activities but may not represent,
  advocate, protect the legitimate rights and interests of legally-aided persons in court; may not sign written legal
  counseling.

  The legal aid trainee may go with the guidance providing legal aid assistant to meet the legally-aided persons
  and other litigants in legal aid-related cases if they agree; assist the legal aid assistant in studying documents
  about the case, collecting documents, items and circumstances relevant to such cases and other professional
  activities. The guidance providing legal aid assistant shall supervise and be responsible for the activities of the
  legal aid trainee as prescribed in this clause.

  3. People exempted from probation of legal profession according to the Law on Lawyers shall be exempted from
  probation of legal aid.

  4. The Minister of Justice shall elaborate probation, probation testing and the form of certificate of legal aid
  training.

  Article 21. Appointment, issuance and re-issuance of legal aid assistant’s card [11]

  1. The Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee shall consider appointment and issuance of a legal aid
  assistant’s card to an eligible legal aid assistant in accordance with Article 19 of this Law if he/she does not fall
  within one of the following cases

  a) He/she is currently incurring a disciplinary penalty; or administrative penalty in a compulsory educational
  institution or rehabilitation center;

  b) He/she is currently facing criminal prosecution; has been convicted of an intentional serious crime, an
  intentional very serious crime, or an intentional extremely serious crime, even if his/her criminal record has been
  expunged; has been convicted of an unintentional very serious crime, an unintentional extremely serious crime,
  or an intentional less serious crime and his/her criminal record has not yet been expunged.

  2. The Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee shall consider appointment and issuance of the legal
  aid assistant’s card to the legal aid assistant who is dismissed or has his/her card revoked in the cases specified in
  point a, dd or g clause 1 Article 22 of this Law when he/she fulfils the conditions specified in Article 19 of this
  Law and reasons for such dismissal and revocation of the card no longer exist.

  3. The Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee shall reissue the legal aid assistant’s card in case it is
  lost or damaged.

  4. The Government shall elaborate this Article, and procedures for appointing, issuing, and reissuing the legal aid
  assistant’s card.

  Article 22. Dismissal and revocation of legal aid assistant’s card [12]

  1. A legal aid assistant shall be dismissed and have his/her legal aid assistant’s card revoked in the following
  cases:

  a) He/she no longer is qualified as a legal aid assistant as prescribed in Article 19 hereof;

  b) He/she does not participate in criminal proceedings within 12 consecutive months except for cases due to
  objective reasons;

  c) He/she is disciplined in the form of forced resignation;

  d) He/she is disciplined in the form of reprimand or higher due to commission of the violation specified in clause
  1 Article 6 of this Law;

  dd) He/she is banned from practicing as a legal aid assistant according to a competent authority’s decision;

  e) He/she is convicted under a legally effective judgment;

  g) He/she incurs administrative penalty in a compulsory educational institution or rehabilitation center.

  2. A legal aid assistant shall be automatically dismissed and his/her legal aid officer card shall automatically
  become invalid in the following cases:

  a) He/she transfers to other jobs; resigns or is forced to resign;

  b) He/she retires.

  3. The Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee shall decide dismissal and revocation of the legal aid
  assistant’s card.

  4. The Government shall elaborate this Article, and procedures for dismissal and revocation of the legal aid
  assistant’s card.

  Article 23. [13] (annulled)

  Article 24. Legal aid collaborators [14]

  1. The following persons may become legal aid collaborators:

   a) Persons who have retired, resigned upon their own aspirations or resigned due to objective reasons; have full
  civil act capacity, good moral qualities, good health and wish to provide legal aid, including: legal aid assistants;
  Judges, inspectors of the court; procurators, inspectors of the Procuracy; investigators; enforcers, examiners in
  civil judgment enforcement; persons holding principal official title/rank or equivalent or higher engaged in legal
  affairs; persons holding official title/rank or equivalent and having at least 05 years of legal affair experience at
  agencies of the Communist Party of Vietnam, the State, the Vietnamese Fatherland Front, and its member
  organizations; or persons who used to be legal aid collaborators;

  b) Public employees holding Grade III title or equivalent and having at least 05 years of legal affair experience,
  or public employees holding Grade I or Grade II title or equivalent, engaged in legal affairs and having obtained
  the written consent of their employers.

  2. The Director of the Department of Justice shall consider issuing a legal aid collaborator’s card to an eligible
  person who meets the conditions specified in clause 1 of this Article and does not fall within one of the
  following cases:

  a) He/she is currently facing criminal prosecution; has been convicted of an intentional serious crime, an
  intentional very serious crime, or an intentional extremely serious crime, even if his/her criminal record has been
  expunged; has been convicted of an unintentional very serious crime, an unintentional extremely serious crime,
  or an intentional less serious crime and his/her criminal record has not yet been expunged;

  b) He/she is currently incurring a disciplinary penalty; or administrative penalty in a compulsory educational
  institution or rehabilitation center;

  3. The Director of the state legal aid center shall sign a contract for provision of legal aid with the person who is
  issued with the legal aid collaborator's card to provide legal consultancy, extrajudicial representation at the

  province.

  4. A legal aid collaborator shall have his/her legal aid collaborator’s card revoked in one of the following cases:

  a) He/she is no longer qualified or no longer meets the conditions specified in clause 1 of this Article;

  b) He/she has not provided legal aid services for 02 consecutive years except for cases due to objective reasons;

  c) He/she commits any of the acts specified in clause 1, Article 6 of this Law, or has incurred administrative
  penalty for violation against regulations on legal aid, but not to the extent that his/her legal aid collaborator's
  card is revoked and he/she continues to commit violations;

  d) The contract for provision of legal aid services is terminated, or the legal aid collaborator fails to enter into a
  contract for provision of legal aid services with the state legal aid center within 30 days from the date of receipt
  of the center's proposal to enter into the contract without a justifiable reason;

  dd) He/she is a public employee who is disciplined in the form of forced resignation;

  e) He/she incurs administrative penalty in a compulsory educational institution or rehabilitation center;

  g) He/she is convicted under a legally effective judgment.

  5. The Director of the Department of Justice shall decide to revoke the legal aid collaborator's card, and reissue
  the legal aid collaborator's card in case it is lost or damaged.

  6. The Government shall elaborate this Article, and procedures for issuing, reissuing and revoking the legal aid
  collaborator's card.

  Article 25. Cases of discontinuance or refusal to provide legal aid services

  1. A legal aid-providing person must not continue to provide legal aid services in the following cases:

  a) Commit the prohibited acts defined in clause 1 Article 6 hereof, except for the case where he/she has
  completely served his/her penalty and is entitled to provide legal aid services according to regulations of this
  Law;

  b) Have his/her legal aid assistant's card, legal aid collaborator’s card, law practicing certificate or legal
  counselor card revoked;

  c) Cases of inability to participate in proceedings as prescribed by law on proceedings.

  2. A legal aid-providing person must refuse to provide legal aid services in one of the following cases:

  a) He/she has provided or is providing legal aid services for a legally-aided person that is a party having
  conflicting interests in the same case, unless otherwise agreed in legal consultancy, extrajudicial representation
  in civil matters by the parties;

  b) There are evidences to believe that he/she is possibly biased during the process of provision of legal aid
  services;

  c) There are reasons that show legal aid services cannot be provided effectively, affecting the legitimate rights
  and interests of legally-aided persons.

  3. The legal aid-providing organization shall notify the reason in writing to the legally-aided person and appoint
  another person to provide legal aid services in the cases specified in clauses 1 and 2 of this Article.

  Chapter V

                                LEGAL AID SCOPE, FIELD, FORM AND SERVICE

  Article 26. Scope of legal aid service

  1. The state legal aid center shall provide legal aid services in one of the following cases:

  a) Legally-aided persons residing at the province;

  b) Legal aid-related cases at the province;

  c) Legal aid-related cases requested by competent central authorities;

  d) [15] Cases transferred in accordance with clause 3 Article 35 of this Law.

  2. Organizations signing contracts to provide legal aid services shall provide legal aid services within these
  contracts.

  3. Organizations registering for participation in provision of legal aid services shall provide legal aid services as
  registered.

  Article 27. Fields and forms of legal aid

  1. Legal aid shall be provided in the fields of law, except for business and trade sector.

  2. Legal aid forms include:

  a) Participation in legal proceedings;

  b) Legal consultancy;

  c) Extrajudicial representation.

  Article 28. Places for reception of legally-aided persons

  1. The legal aid-providing organization shall arrange places for reception of legally-aided persons at its head
  office of such organization or a place other than the head office which is convenient for legally-aided persons to
  express their requests.

  2. Timetable and internal rules on reception of legally-aided persons must be posted at the legal aid-providing
  organization’s head office.

  Article 29. [16] (annulled)

  Article 30. Request and acceptance of legal aid-related cases [17]

  1. When requesting legal aid, the legally-aided person must submit an application to the legal aid-providing
  organization.

  2. The legal aid request shall only be accepted when there are specific cases directly related to the legitimate
  rights and interests of the legally-aided person according to regulations of this Law.

  3. The legal aid-providing organization must refuse the request and clearly state the reasons in writing to the
  requester in one of the following cases:

  a) The legal aid request fails to satisfy one of the conditions prescribed in clause 2 this Article;

  b) The legal aid request contains illegal contents;

  c) The legally-aided person dies;

  d) The case is accepted and settled by another legal aid-providing organization;

  dd) The legal aid request has been resolved and no new matter arises.

  4. In case the requester cannot provide sufficient documents but the legal aid is immediately required due to the
  fact that the legal aid-related case was about to be expired or the trial day is approaching, the case requiring legal
  aid is transferred to the legal aid-providing organization by the authority having jurisdiction to institute
  proceedings or the presiding agency or for the purpose of avoiding damage to the legitimate rights and interests
  of the legally-aided person, the recipient shall notify the head of the legal aid-providing organization and accept
  the case immediately, at the same time provide guidance for the requester to provide additionally necessary
  documentation.

  5. The Minister of Justice shall elaborate this Article; and procedures for acceptance, immediate acceptance, and
  refusal of acceptance of legal aid-related cases.

  Article 31. Participation in legal proceedings

  1. Legal aid assistants, lawyers providing legal aid services shall participate in legal proceedings in the capacity
  of defenders or protectors of legally-aided persons’ legitimate rights and interests in accordance with this Law
  and the Law on Proceedings.

  2. Within 03 working days from the date of receipt of legally-aided persons' requests for the appointment of legal
  aid-providing persons to participate in legal proceedings, legal aid-providing organizations shall appoint legal
  aid- providing persons.

  Within 12 hours from the time of receipt of a request from the legally-aided person who is arrested or detained
  for the appointment of a legal aid-providing person, the legal aid-providing organization shall appoint the legal
  aid-providing person.

  3. Within 12 hours from the time of receipt of a request from a person who is arrested or detained or within 24
  hours from the time of receipt of a request from a legally-aided person who is suspect, defendant, victim
  according to the Law on Proceedings, the authority/person having jurisdiction to institute proceedings shall
  notify the state legal aid center at the province. Immediately after receiving the notification from the
  authority/person having jurisdiction to institute proceedings, the state legal aid center shall accept the case as
  prescribed in clause 4 Article 30 hereof and appoint a legal aid-providing person to participate in legal
  proceedings.

  4. The appointment of representatives beyond legal proceedings must be expressed in a document to be sent to
  the concerned legally-aided person and presiding agency.

  Article 32. Legal consultancy [18]

  1. Persons may provide legal aid in counseling for legally-aided persons by giving guidance, giving opinions,
  helping draft documents related to disputes, complaints and legal problems; giving guidance on mediation,
  negotiation and agreement on settling the case.

  2. The Minister of Justice shall elaborate this Article; and procedures for provision of legal counseling.

  Article 33. Extrajudicial representation [19]

  1. Legal aid assistants, lawyers providing legal aid and legal aid collaborators shall act as extrajudicial
  representatives before competent regulatory agencies for legally-aided persons.

  2. The Minister of Justice shall elaborate this Article; and procedures for extrajudicial representation.

  Article 34. Cooperation in verification of legal aid-related cases [20]

  1. When it is necessary to verify details and events related to a legal aid-related case in another administrative
  division, the legal aid-providing organization which has accepted the case may request the legal aid-providing
  organization in such administrative division to cooperate in the verification. A verification request must be made
  in writing, clearly stating the contents to be verified and the deadline for reply.

  2. The Minister of Justice shall elaborate this Article; and procedures for cooperation in verification of legal aid-
  related cases.

  Article 35. Transfer of legal aid request and legal aid-related cases [21]

  1. In case the legal aid request fails to satisfy the conditions specified in points a and b clause 1 Article 26
  hereof, the state legal aid center shall transfer such legal aid request to competent state legal aid center and notify
  the concerned legally-aided person.

  2. In case of insufficient resources for provision of legal aid service, the legal aid-participating organization shall
  transfer such legal aid request to state legal aid center at the province and notify the concerned legally-aided
  person.

  3. [22] The state legal aid center currently handling a legal aid-related case may transfer such case to a state legal
  aid center in another administrative division when the legal aid-related case has been transferred to and handled
  by the authority having jurisdiction to institute proceedings or the presiding agency in such administrative
  division, and shall notify the legally-aided person.

  Article 36. Recommendation in legal aid services [23]

  1. During provision of legal aid services, legal aid-providing organizations may send written recommendations
  to competent regulatory agencies about matters related to handling of legal aid-related cases. Agencies receiving
  written recommendations shall, within the scope of their tasks and powers, be responsible for responding in
  writing in accordance with regulations of law.

  2. In case agencies receiving written recommendations fail to respond in accordance with regulations of clause 1
  of this Article, legal aid-providing organizations are entitled to request their direct superior agencies to consider
  resolution.

  3. The Government shall elaborate this Article, and procedures for recommendation in legal aid services

  Article 37. Discontinuation in provision of legal aid services

  1. Legal aid-related cases shall be discontinued in one of the following cases:

  a) Cases of refusal according to regulations of clause 3, Article 30 of this Law;

  b) The legally-aided person commits one of the acts prohibited as prescribed in clause 2 Article 6 hereof;

  c) The legally-aided person withdraws his/her request for legal aid.

  2. In case of discontinuance of the provision or legal aid, the legal aid-providing organization or person shall
  notify the reason in writing to the legally-aided person.

  3. If a legal aid-related case is being carried out but the legally-aided person no longer satisfies the provisions of
  Article 7 hereof, such case shall continue being carried out until the end.

  Article 38. Dossiers of legal aid-related cases [24]

  When providing legal aid, legal aid-providing organizations and persons shall compile dossiers of legal aid-
  related cases according to regulations issued by the Minister of Justice.

  Article 39. Storage of dossiers of legal aid-related cases

  1. Within 30 days after finishing a legal aid-related case, the legal aid-providing person shall transfer the dossier
  to the legal aid-providing organization.

  2. Documents and papers included in the dossier of legal aid-related cases must be registered, numbered and
  arranged in the order of date, month, year and stored according to the law.

  3. Electronic dossier of each legal aid-related case shall be digitized and updated to the legal aid-related case
  management system and stored in the database of legal aid.

  Chapter VI

      RESPONSIBILITIES OF AGENCIES, ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS FOR LEGAL AID
                                       SERVICES

  Article 40. Responsibilities for state management of legal aid

  1. The Government shall perform the uniform state management of legal aid.

  2. The Ministry of Justice is a focal point to assist the Government in performing state management of legal aid
  and has the following tasks and powers:

  a) Take charge of formulation of, promulgate or request competent regulatory agencies to promulgate legislative
  documents on legal aid;

  b) Formulate, promulgate or request competent authorities to promulgate strategies and plans for the
  development of legal aid services and organize the implementation of these strategies and plans;

  c) [25] Promulgate regulations and guidance on professional expertise, operations, assessment of the quality and
  efficiency in legal aid-related cases; specimen papers used in legal aid services; criteria for identification of
  complex, typical, high-quality, or successful legal aid-related cases; and make reports and statistics on legal aid
  services; <0}

  d) Provide guidance, organize and follow the implementation of legislative documents on legal aid;

  dd) Organize training in legal aid knowledge and skills for legal aid-providing persons;

  e) Organize communication on legal aid [26];

  g) [27] Inspect the provision of legal aid services; reward, discipline and handle violations against regulations on
  provision of legal aid services;

  h) Receive support and contributions from organizations and individuals for legal aid;

  i) Implement international cooperation in legal aid;

  k) [28] Apply information technology and digital technology, and develop digital transformation in legal aid
  service; build, manage, operate, and regularly upgrade the legal aid information system and database; connect,
  integrate and share legal aid data on the national law portal.

  3. [29] Ministries and ministerial-level agencies shall, within their tasks and powers, be responsible for
  cooperating with the Ministry of Justice in state management and organization of provision of legal aid service;
  and creating, integrating, sharing, accessing, and using data through connection and inter-linkage with the legal
  aid database on the national law portal.

  4. [30] Provincial People's Committees shall, within their tasks and powers, perform state management of legal
  aid in their province, maintain working conditions for state legal aid centers, and cooperate with the Ministry of
  Justice in creating, integrating, sharing, accessing, and using data through connection and inter-linkage with the
  legal aid database on the national law portal.

  5. [31] Commune-level People's Committees shall cooperate with state legal aid centers in providing legal aid
  services within their communes.

  6. [32]The Government elaborates this Article.

  Article 41. Responsibilities of agencies related to legal aid services in legal proceedings [33]

  1. Within their tasks and powers, authorities having jurisdiction to institute proceedings and presiding agencies
  shall be responsible for cooperating and organizing cooperation in implementation of inter-branch mechanisms
  and provision of legal aid services, in person at People's Courts and during criminal investigations; enable
  legally-aided persons entitled to receive legal aid services and legal aid-providing persons to participate in legal
  proceedings according to regulations.

  2. The Minister of Justice, the Chief Justice of the Supreme People's Court, the Prosecutor General of the
  Supreme People's Procuracy, the Minister of National Defense, the Minister of Public Security, and the Minister
  of Finance shall cooperate in establishing an inter-branch cooperation council mechanism for legal aid services
  in legal proceedings at both central and provincial levels.

  3. Agencies related to legal aid services in legal proceedings shall be responsible for cooperating with the
  Ministry of Justice in creating, integrating, sharing, accessing, and using data through connection and inter-
  linkage with the legal aid database on the national law portal.

  Article 42. Responsibilities of Vietnamese Fatherland Front, its member organizations, and relevant
  regulatory agencies [34]

  1. The Vietnamese Fatherland Front and its member organizations shall, within their functions and tasks,
  supervise the implementation of policies and laws on legal aid, and cooperate with relevant regulatory agencies
  and organizations in provision of legal aid services in accordance with regulations of law.

  2. During handling and resolution of cases involved in citizens, if such citizens are eligible for legal aid,
  regulatory agencies shall be responsible for explaining their rights to receive legal aid services and referring
  them to legal aid-providing organizations.

  Article 43. Responsibilities of socio-professional organizations of lawyers

  1. The Vietnam Bar Federation shall cooperate with the Ministry of Justice in managing and supervising the
  provision of legal aid services by lawyers and law-practicing organizations in accordance with this Law.

  2. Bar Federations of centrally-affiliated cities and provinces shall cooperate with Departments of Justice to
  manage and supervise the provision of legal aid services by lawyers and law-practicing organizations in

  accordance with this Law.

  Article 44. Responsibilities of agency directly supervising legal counseling organizations

  The agency directly supervising legal counseling organizations shall cooperate with competent legal aid
  authorities in managing and supervising provision of legal aid services by legal consulting firms and legal
  consultants in accordance with this Law.

  Chapter VII

                   SETTLEMENT OF COMPLAINTS, DENUNCIATIONS AND DISPUTES

  Article 45. Settlement of complaints and denunciations

  1. Legally-aided persons may lodge complaints about the following acts committed by legal aid-providing
  organizations, legal aid-providing persons when there are grounds to believe that such acts are unlawful acts or
  infringe upon their legitimate rights and interests:

  a) Refuse to accept legal aid-related cases;

  b) Fail to provide legal aid services;

  c) Provide illegal legal aid services;

  d) Change legal aid-providing person illegally.

  2. [35] Heads of legal aid-providing organizations shall settle complaints about the acts specified in clause 1 this
  Article. If the complainants disagree with complaint-settlement decisions issued by heads of legal aid-providing
  organizations or upon the expiration of the deadline, if the complaints are not resolved, they may further lodge
  their complaints to Directors of Departments of Justice.

  If the complainants disagree with complaint-settlement decisions issued by Directors of Departments of Justice
  or upon the expiration of the deadline, if the complaints are not resolved, they may file lawsuits in Courts.

  The Government shall elaborate this clause, and procedures for settlement of complaints about legal aid.

  3. [36] Complaints and lawsuits against legal aid other than those specified in clause 1 of this Article shall be
  settled in accordance with regulations of the law on complaints and other relevant provisions of law.

  4. Individuals may denounce violations against this Law to competent regulatory agencies. Denunciations and
  settlement of denunciations shall comply with the law on denunciations.

  Article 46. Settlement of disputes

  1. Disputes arising between legally-aided persons and legal aid assistants, legal counselors, legal aid
  collaborators, state legal aid centers or legal counseling organizations related to the provision of legal aid
  services shall be settled in accordance with the civil law.

  2. Disputes arising between legally-aided persons and lawyers or law practicing organizations related to the
  provision of legal aid services shall be settled in accordance with the law on lawyers and other relevant laws.

  Chapter VIII

                                           IMPLEMENTATION CLAUSES [37]

  Article 47. Effect

  1. This Law takes effect on January 1, 2018.

  2. The Law on Legal Aid No. 69/2006/QH11 shall become invalid since this Law takes effect.

  Article 48. Transitional provisions

  1. From the effective date of this Law, the persons who have been appointed as legal aid assistants under the Law
  on Legal Aid No. 69/2006/QH11 shall continue to operate under the provisions of this Law; after 05 years from
  the effective date of this Law, the persons who are appointed as legal aid assistants without certificates certifying
  graduates of lawyer training shall have their legal aid assistant cards revoked.

  2. Within 01 year from the effective date of this Law, legal aid-participating organizations and individuals
  according to the Law on Legal Aid No. 69/2006/QH11 must satisfy the requirements of this Law. If they fail to
  satisfy the requirements of this Law, they shall terminate their participation in legal aid services and transfer the
  dossiers of the cases currently carried out to state legal aid centers where they register for participation to
  continue their provision.

  3. Legal aid-related cases that are currently carried out under the Law on Legal Aid No. 69/2006/QH11 but by
  the date this law takes effect they are not yet completed, they shall continue to be carried out in accordance with
  the Law on Legal Aid No. 69/2006/QH11 until the completion of such cases.

  4. Within 01 year from the effective date of this Law, provincial People's Committees shall review the branches
  of state legal aid centers established in their respective provinces and, base on the needs, resources of legal aid
  and the efficiency, report to the Ministry of Justice to unify the maintenance, merger or dissolution of branches
  of state legal aid centers.
